findings.evidence: ALTER TABLE users DROP COLUMN legacy_email;
findings.recommendation: Running migration 0005 on production permanently deletes every value in users.legacy_email. There is no 0005_drop_legacy_email.down.sql (unlike 0004, which has 0004_accounts.down.sql), and neither the proposal nor tasks.md has a backup or recovery step; task 1.1 only checks that `sqlx migrate run` succeeds. Add a down migration that re-adds the column (`ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN legacy_email TEXT;`), and add a step that exports `id, legacy_email` (or snapshots the table) before the drop. Otherwise, say in the plan that the data is deliberately abandoned and how to recover it from backups. Also confirm no running instance still reads the column before the drop ships (contract only after the code no longer uses it).
findings.title: Irreversible column drop with no down migration or backup

findings.recommendation: `Account` is a type of the public HTTP API (src/api.rs: "The JSON types of the public HTTP API."). Every existing client that reads `user_name` from the account endpoint gets a missing field after deploy: it reads undefined/null, or fails to deserialize. The proposal's release note only says "Changed: Account JSON uses camelCase." with no **BREAKING** mark and nothing on what clients must do, and no deprecation period. Mark the item **BREAKING** in the release note with the old and new name and the required client change. Give consumers time: emit both `user_name` and `userName` for one release (e.g. a second serialized field or a custom Serialize), deprecate `user_name`, then remove it, or version the endpoint.
findings.title: Account JSON field renamed to userName without a BREAKING mark or compatibility path
